status: REGISTERED before engine installation and experimental execution
question: Can a pinned mature Python 2D engine provide stable articulated wheel and moving-bridge fixtures with usable measured offscreen throughput on this workstation?
scope: Synthetic engineering fixtures only; no game fidelity, calibration, policy learning or transfer qualification
rapid_learning_authority: Primary outcome is elapsed command time to independently evaluated real-game competence. This engine pilot has no competence observation. Compute, simulated experience, episode counts and wall time remain separate costs; raw rates never select the final method.
observation_recording: Each completed diagnostic repeat, diagnostic gate and throughput arm is immediately stored as an exclusive immutable engine-observation-3.0 JSON artifact. Completed measurements survive a later failed gate or arm. These fixtures have no episode lifecycle: training/evaluation/real-game episode counts remain zero; scripted fixture decisions are separate and no EvaluationRecord is emitted.

candidate.installation: Fresh run-local target directory; binary wheel only, no dependencies, hash required; stdout/stderr, pip report, installed binary and notices retained

alternatives.box2d-python-0.1.2: Box2D 3 CFFI binding with CPython 3.13 Windows wheel, MIT wrapper, Python>=3.12 and explicitly preview API. Consider a second bounded pilot if the mature binding has a measured limitation; not rejected by uncollected performance evidence.
alternatives.surrogate-0.1.0: Preserved legacy comparator; its two virtual contacts and heightfield cannot represent the articulated fixtures. Raw speed comparison would therefore measure different workloads.

fixture_parameters: Original synthetic constants encoded in the committed fixture source. No proprietary coefficients or game assets. One chassis, two independently rotating wheel bodies, spring/damper wheel joints, independent drive torque and brake motor. Bridge has twelve collidable planks and thirteen revolute joints over an actual ground gap.

screen.action_sequence: Gas for the first 70% of decisions then brake; this is a diagnostic script, never a learned driver

checks: body speed and angular speed bounds
diagnostics.limits_interpretation: Prospective synthetic sanity limits, not tolerances for real-game fidelity or a claim of physically identified parameters

pilot_clock_definition: Pilot elapsed time starts after protocol/source verification and includes installation, fixture construction, diagnostics and measurements; caller imports and final artifact serialization/sealing are separate overhead. It is not a command-start learning clock or rapid-learning result.
stopping_rule: Stop on installation failure, nonfinite state, invalid engine version, or a failed diagnostic gate; retain the failed canonical run. Incomplete throughput arms remain censored at their wall cap, not discarded or replaced. At most one screen under this protocol; further screens need a linked prospective amendment.
selection_rule: An engineering candidate can proceed to measured fixture construction only if installation and all diagnostic gates pass and at least one rendered arm completes within its cap. Report every throughput arm; select no learning algorithm, final batch size or fidelity level from FPS. Subsequent fixed-source comparisons must justify added fidelity/compute through independent real competence and report Pareto comparisons of real performance, wall time, experience and compute with explicit prior cost.
source_authority: Execute only after the implementation and this protocol are committed, with exact expected SHA and clean source. No concurrent edits or unrelated high-load jobs during timing; disclose any observed concurrent load.
